title: The Return of the Taiwan Tiger - The Wire China
gist: The U.S. now imports more from Taiwan ($116.1 billion in the first five months of 2026) than from China including Hong Kong ($105.5 billion), the first such reversal since 1992, driven by an AI capex wave of $750 billion to $1 trillion from U.S. hyperscalers and by TSMC, whose ~$2 trillion market cap is more than double Taiwan's GDP and 44 percent of the Taiwan Stock Exchange. The offsetting risks are a missing U.S.-Taiwan tax treaty leaving a 51 percent effective rate on Taiwanese U.S. profits, a $30 billion undelivered arms backlog plus a KMT-gutted defense budget that stripped all $15 billion earmarked for drones and air defense, and Taiwan's power, water and super-aged demographic constraints.

insights.claim: Taiwan exported $116.1 billion in goods and services to the United States in the first five months of 2026 versus $105.5 billion from China including Hong Kong, meaning the U.S. now imports more from Taiwan than from China.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: A 23.4 million-person economy outselling a 1.4 billion-person one into the U.S. marks a structural rerouting of supply chains worth tracking through Taiwanese export orders as a China-substitution gauge.
insights.quote: The U.S. is now importing more from Taiwan than it does from China.
insights.locator: As the world prepares for an AI future

insights.claim: The last time U.S. imports from Taiwan exceeded those from China was 1992, when China's economy was only about twice the size of Taiwan's; it is now 21 times bigger, making the reversal far more extreme than the 1992 precedent.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: The 21x GDP gap quantifies just how concentrated the value is in Taiwan's export mix — essentially semiconductors — and how narrow the base of the flip is.
insights.locator: The last time this happened was 1992

insights.claim: The United States has displaced China as Taiwan's top trading partner, reversing a 2016 position in which Taiwan-U.S. trade totaled $85 billion against $180 billion in Taiwan-China trade.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: A complete inversion of Taiwan's trade orientation in under a decade reduces Beijing's economic coercion leverage over Taipei and raises Washington's.
insights.locator: The U.S. has also displaced China as Taiwan’s top trading partner

insights.claim: A senior U.S. diplomat speaking anonymously said Taiwan moved from being America's tenth-largest trading partner ten years ago to number four today, just behind China, that the U.S. is Taiwan's top investment destination, and that American firms are the largest investors in Taiwan.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Rank four with two-way investment leadership means Taiwan-specific disruption would now hit U.S. corporate earnings directly, not just component supply.
insights.quote: U.S.-Taiwan trade and investment relations have completely transformed in substance and structure
insights.locator: one senior U.S. diplomat told The Wire

themes.theme: AI Capex Wave Powers Taiwan Growth

insights.claim: America's biggest technology companies including Apple, Microsoft, Amazon Web Services, Google, Oracle and Meta are spending between $750 billion and $1 trillion combined on AI infrastructure in 2026 alone, according to Rupert Hammond-Chambers of the U.S.-Taiwan Business Council.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Puts a hard number on the demand pool feeding Taiwan's hardware ecosystem; any hyperscaler capex deceleration transmits almost immediately to Taiwanese GDP.
insights.locator: America’s biggest technology companies including Apple

insights.claim: Taiwan's economy grew 14.6 percent in the first quarter of 2026 versus the same period in 2025, driven primarily by AI-related exports and knock-on effects in investment, the stock market and consumer spending — against growth of less than two percent per annum ten years ago.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Double-digit growth in a mature high-income economy is an AI-cycle artifact, so treat Taiwanese macro prints as a high-beta read on AI hardware demand rather than a durable trend.
insights.locator: In the first quarter of this year, Taiwan’s economy grew 14.6 percent

insights.claim: A senior U.S. diplomat described Taiwan as America's most important international partner in the AI sector because pretty much every piece of hardware is manufactured by a Taiwan company, and said Taiwan plays a similar role in drones because it can replace Chinese components at scale.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Taiwan as the designated non-China drone component source is an underpriced second leg to the Taiwan trade beyond semiconductors.
insights.quote: Taiwan is our most important international partner in the AI sector — pretty much every piece of hardware is manufactured by a Taiwan company
insights.locator: “Taiwan is our most important international partner in the AI sector

insights.claim: U.S.-Taiwan cooperation is being deliberately expanded into quantum computing, robotics and critical minerals — especially critical minerals recycling — according to a senior U.S. diplomat.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Names the next three sectors where U.S.-Taiwan industrial policy money and MOUs are likely to land, a forward map for early positioning.
insights.quote: We are now focused on expanding cooperation to new sectors like quantum computing, robotics and critical minerals — especially critical minerals recycling.
insights.locator: We are now focused on expanding cooperation to new sectors

insights.claim: TSMC's market capitalization is around $2 trillion, more than double Taiwan's projected GDP for 2026, and it accounts for more than 44 percent of the entire value of the Taiwan Stock Exchange — itself the world's fifth-biggest bourse after recently surpassing India and the UK.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Extreme single-name index concentration means Taiwan equity exposure is effectively a levered TSMC position; hedge accordingly.
insights.locator: The company’s market capitalization is currently around $2 trillion

insights.claim: TSMC is now the world's sixth most-valuable company and an irreplaceable partner for almost all of the other companies in the global top 10, nine of which are technology firms with Saudi Arabia's Aramco the sole exception.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Frames TSMC as a systemic dependency for the entire mega-cap tech complex, meaning a Taiwan disruption is a global index event rather than a sector event.
insights.locator: TSMC is now the world’s sixth most-valuable company

insights.claim: On July 16, 2026 TSMC announced an additional $100 billion for its Arizona campus, raising total planned U.S. investment to $265 billion and making it the biggest foreign investor in the United States, up from an initial $12 billion commitment in 2020.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: A 22x escalation in six years is the clearest evidence of onshoring momentum and a direct read on Arizona construction, power and semiconductor-equipment demand.
insights.locator: On July 16, TSMC announced it will plow an additional $100 billion

insights.claim: TSMC's planned 2026 capital expenditure is $62 billion — twice Taiwan's entire annual defense budget.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: The capex-versus-defense-budget ratio captures the core asymmetry: Taiwan's economic crown jewel outspends its own deterrence by 2x, which is a political argument that will keep recurring.
insights.quote: Its planned 2026 capex outlay is $62 billion — twice Taiwan’s annual defense budget.
insights.locator: Its planned 2026 capex outlay is $62 billion

insights.claim: Rupert Hammond-Chambers argues the essential difference in Taiwan's fortunes is the emergence of TSMC as the world's indispensable technology company, making Taiwan the pivot point in the U.S.-China great-power technology competition.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: A single-company explanation for a national economic revival is also a single point of failure — the key framework for sizing Taiwan concentration risk.
insights.quote: In the great-power technology competition between the U.S. and China, Taiwan is the pivot point in the battle.
insights.locator: “The essential difference is the emergence of TSMC

themes.theme: Trade Deal Done, Tax Treaty Missing

insights.claim: The Agreement on Reciprocal Trade concluded between Taiwan's Lai administration and Trump in February 2026 set tariffs on Taiwan's exports to the U.S. at 15 percent, the same level imposed on Japan and South Korea.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Tariff parity with Japan and Korea removes a relative-disadvantage overhang for Taiwanese exporters and is the settled baseline for margin modeling.
insights.locator: Momentum in the U.S.-Taiwan economic relationship has been further enhanced

insights.claim: In the absence of a U.S.-Taiwan tax treaty, Taipei estimates the effective tax rate on Taiwanese companies' U.S. profits is 51 percent, citing withholding charges on repatriated dividends.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: A 51 percent effective rate is the single largest identified friction on Taiwanese investment into the U.S.; treaty passage would be a material earnings catalyst for Taiwanese firms with U.S. operations.
insights.locator: Taipei has estimated the effective tax rate

insights.claim: Taiwan and Vietnam are the only two of America's top-10 trading partners without a double-tax treaty, a gap that matters most for Taiwan's 1.7 million small and medium-sized enterprises which employ almost 80 percent of the country's workforce.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: The SME channel is where a tax treaty would unlock a new wave of first-time U.S. expansion, an underfollowed second-order beneficiary of ratification.
insights.locator: Taiwan and Vietnam, Chen notes, are the only two

insights.claim: AmCham Taiwan chair Anita Chen, who also heads Google's government relations team in Taipei, said procedural hurdles remain for launching a U.S.-Taiwan double-tax treaty by the end of 2026 even though the agreement is awaiting passage on Capitol Hill.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
entities: American Chamber of Commerce in Taiwan
insights.so_what: Treat end-2026 tax treaty passage as uncertain rather than base case; the Capitol Hill calendar is the thing to monitor.
insights.locator: That said, Chen, who also heads Google’s government relations team

insights.claim: The American Chamber of Commerce in Taiwan's June 2026 annual White Paper hailed a 'golden age in U.S.-Taiwan economic relations' and cited overwhelming bipartisan support for Taiwan in Congress alongside strong recognition of Taiwan's value in the administration.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
entities: American Chamber of Commerce in Taiwan
insights.so_what: Bipartisan durability means the Taiwan economic relationship is relatively insulated from U.S. election cycles, lowering the political risk discount on Taiwan-linked capex.
insights.quote: golden age in U.S.-Taiwan economic relations
insights.locator: In its recently published annual White Paper

insights.claim: Taiwan's energy security and power supply are a perennial problem now exacerbated by the growing number of power-hungry chip fabs under construction on the island, while climate-driven droughts and chip industry consumption drain reservoirs.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Power and water are the physical ceilings on Taiwan's fab expansion, which strengthens the case for offshore capacity in Arizona and Japan.
insights.locator: Energy security and power supply is a perennial problem

insights.claim: Taiwan's heavy government subsidy of power use leads to wasteful consumption and disincentivizes state-owned Taipower and other power companies from investing in infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Subsidy-driven underinvestment means grid capex will lag fab demand until tariffs are reformed — a recurring outage and curtailment risk for chip production.
insights.locator: Taiwan’s government heavily subsidizes power use

insights.claim: Rupert Hammond-Chambers argues Taiwan's approach to power supply, infrastructure and production remains far too reactive and that the government needs a long-term grid investment plan, ideally funded through a special budget outside the regular annual budget given the amounts required.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: A special grid budget would be a large, identifiable order flow for transmission and generation equipment suppliers; watch for it in Taiwan's legislative agenda.
insights.quote: Taiwan’s approach to power supply, infrastructure and production remains far too reactive
insights.locator: “Taiwan’s approach to power supply, infrastructure and production

insights.claim: Taiwan's birth rate has fallen below replacement level and the island entered the ranks of 'super-aged' societies last year, defined as those where 20 percent or more of citizens are 65 or older.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Super-aged status caps the domestic labor supply for fab and construction expansion, making immigration liberalization a gating factor for Taiwan's AI-cycle capacity.
insights.locator: Lastly, and like the rest of East Asia

themes.theme: Taiwan's Investment Pivot Away From China

insights.claim: Fifteen years ago more than 80 percent of Taiwanese outbound investment went to China; today that figure is less than one percent.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: A near-total collapse from 80 percent to under 1 percent is the most striking decoupling statistic in the piece and reframes Taiwan's exposure to Chinese economic coercion as minimal.
insights.quote: Fifteen years ago, more than 80 percent of Taiwanese outbound investment went to China. Today that figure is less than one percent.
insights.locator: TAIWAN’S U.S. PIVOT

insights.claim: John Deng, Taiwan's chief trade negotiator during the Tsai administration, says U.S.-Taiwan arrangements have moved from shared goals and principles a decade ago to practical cooperation in cybersecurity, talent exchange, supply chain resilience and joint efforts in third countries, with investment now flowing in both directions at rapidly growing scale.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Bidirectional investment plus third-country joint efforts means Taiwanese manufacturing capital is now a competitor for the same projects Western firms bid on.
insights.quote: Today investment flows in both directions. Taiwanese companies are increasingly investing and manufacturing in the United States, with rapidly growing scale.
insights.locator: “A decade ago, the U.S. and Taiwan’s bilateral arrangements

insights.claim: More than a dozen new U.S. trade and investment offices have opened in Taipei in the last several years, with Oklahoma opening one on July 3, 2026 — the same day Taiwan announced it intends to open an economic and cultural office, similar to a consulate, in Arizona.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Sub-national office proliferation is a leading indicator of where Taiwanese greenfield investment lands next; track state-level trade office openings.
insights.locator: “States across the United States are now competing

insights.claim: Channing Lee of the Special Competitive Studies Project argues Taiwan's lack of official recognition as a country has actually allowed state-level engagement to flourish because MOUs, investment deals and university exchanges do not require top-down oversight from Washington or Taipei.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Counterintuitive framing: diplomatic non-recognition is a feature that decentralizes and accelerates deal-making, so ignore federal-level signaling as the sole gauge of ties.
insights.quote: Taiwan’s lack of official recognition as a country has allowed state-level engagement to flourish
insights.locator: “Taiwan’s lack of official recognition as a country

insights.claim: TSMC has moved more than 2,000 engineers and their families to Phoenix, driving a wave of Taiwanese eateries and cafes in the city's north, and Taiwanese carrier Starlux launched Taoyuan-Phoenix flights in January 2026 as the city's second direct Taipei connection after China Airlines, while EVA Air launched the first direct Washington-Taipei flights in late June.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: New long-haul routes and engineer relocation are hard physical confirmation that the onshoring is real, and a demand tailwind for Taiwanese carriers and Phoenix-area real estate.
insights.locator: The number of direct flights between the U.S. and Taiwan

themes.theme: Defense Gap and the Drone Dispute

insights.claim: Trump has been far less explicit than Biden about willingness to defend Taiwan, is delaying approval of a $14 billion arms package, and referred to Taiwan as a 'good negotiating chip' after his May 2026 meeting with Xi Jinping in Beijing.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Strategic-ambiguity drift plus a stalled $14 billion package is the main geopolitical risk premium input for Taiwan assets, even as the economic relationship deepens.
insights.locator: Despite Donald Trump’s reference to Taiwan as a “good negotiating chip”

insights.claim: There is currently a $30 billion backlog of fully approved but still undelivered U.S. weapons systems for which Taipei has already paid, even though Trump has approved substantially more arms sales to Taiwan than his predecessors.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: A $30 billion paid-but-undelivered backlog is a U.S. defense-industrial capacity problem as much as a policy one, and a revenue-recognition overhang at the primes.
insights.locator: While Trump has approved substantially more arms sales

insights.claim: The KMT-controlled legislature stripped all of the funds from Lai Ching-te's special defense budget earmarked for drones and air defense — $15 billion of a proposed $40 billion over eight years — with the budget proposed in November and passed only in June.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Removal of the entire drone and air-defense allocation kills the near-term Taiwan order pipeline for exactly the systems that proved decisive in Ukraine.
insights.quote: The KMT stripped all of those funds from the budget.
insights.locator: Arguably more concerning for Taiwan’s defense needs

insights.claim: KMT chair Cheng Li-wun argues a Taiwanese defense buildup could threaten peace in the Taiwan Strait, and she met Xi Jinping in Beijing in April 2026 where she echoed his claims that Taiwan is an inalienable part of China and that Taiwanese independence cannot be tolerated.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: The opposition holding the legislature is now openly aligned with Beijing's framing, making Taiwan's defense procurement hostage to domestic politics through at least the next election.
insights.locator: The KMT’s new chair, Cheng Li-wun

insights.claim: Taiwan's National Chung-Shan Institute of Science and Technology has signed cooperation and development agreements with seven U.S. defense tech firms including Anduril Industries and MARTAC, covering AI-enabled command and control systems and naval drones.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
entities: National Chung-Shan Institute of Science and Technology
insights.so_what: Defense-tech startups are displacing legacy primes as Taiwan's development partners, a concrete channel for Anduril-class firms to book Indo-Pacific programs.
insights.locator: While the Lockheed Martins and Raytheons drag their feet

insights.claim: Cathy Fang of the Taiwan government-funded think tank DSET says the previous buyer-seller relationship between Taiwan's military and U.S. defense contractors is changing toward software-hardware integration, platform adaptation and AI-enabled mission capability.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: A shift from procurement to co-development changes the margin profile and lock-in of U.S.-Taiwan defense contracts in favor of software-heavy vendors.
insights.quote: It is beginning to involve software-hardware integration, platform adaptation and AI-enabled mission capability.
insights.locator: “Cooperation is no longer limited to supplier relationships,”

insights.claim: Taiwan's drone industry association TEDIBOA has signed six cooperation agreements with U.S. industry, government and academic institutions explicitly aimed at reducing the industry's current reliance on China-based suppliers.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Concrete institutional plumbing for a non-China drone supply chain, the sector where Taiwanese component substitution is most immediately monetizable.
insights.locator: Taiwan’s drone industry association

insights.claim: Cathy Fang says U.S. defense firms are unlikely to commit capital, personnel, tooling or production know-how to Taiwan-based manufacturing unless Taiwan provides a stable multi-year demand signal, and that signal remains incomplete because the KMT is still blocking Taiwan's major drone-related funding package in the legislature.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: The gating variable for U.S. defense-industrial investment in Taiwan is legislative, not commercial — watch the KMT-controlled legislature, not Pentagon announcements.
insights.quote: U.S. defense firms are unlikely to commit capital, personnel, tooling, or production know-how to Taiwan-based manufacturing unless Taiwan provides a stable multi-year demand signal.
insights.locator: “U.S. defense firms are unlikely to commit capital

insights.claim: Core operational questions such as how U.S. and Taiwanese drones would share data and operate together remain unresolved, and without joint testing, shared data standards, pre-positioned weapons stocks and joint exercises the two forces are more likely to operate in parallel than as an integrated force.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Interoperability, not hardware volume, is the binding constraint on allied combat effectiveness; joint data-standard announcements would be the real progress marker.
insights.locator: But in terms of actual military-to-military coordination

insights.claim: John Deng argues the main obstacle to a U.S.-Taiwan free trade agreement is political rather than economic, because some U.S. policymakers fear Chinese retaliation that could significantly hit American industries still reliant on the Chinese market.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Identifies which U.S. constituencies block an FTA — China-exposed industries — so their exposure trends are the leading indicator for whether an FTA becomes viable.
insights.quote: The main obstacle, in my view, is political rather than economic
insights.locator: A TAIWAN-U.S. FTA?

insights.claim: Ma Ying-jeou's unpopular attempt to open Taiwan's service sector to Chinese investment sparked the 2014 Sunflower protests, which helped the DPP's Tsai Ing-wen win the 2016 presidential election.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Historical precedent that cross-strait economic opening is electorally toxic in Taiwan, capping how far a KMT legislature can actually push integration with China.
insights.locator: His unpopular attempt to open up Taiwan’s service sector

insights.claim: John Deng proposes that rather than moving directly to formal FTA negotiations, Washington and Taipei could begin with a six- or twelve-month joint feasibility study, which would also give both sides time to prepare support measures for industries targeted by Chinese retaliation.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: A feasibility study is the realistic next observable step; its announcement would be the earliest tradeable signal of FTA momentum.
insights.locator: Deng adds that rather than moving directly into formal negotiations

insights.claim: John Deng frames deeper U.S.-Taiwan commercial ties as deterrence, arguing that any action threatening Taiwan would also threaten American investments, supply chains and the interests of U.S. companies.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: The economic-entanglement-as-deterrence thesis is the core investment case for why Taiwan risk may be lower than headlines imply — but it depends on entanglement continuing to deepen.
insights.quote: Deeper commercial ties send a very clear message to China: the United States has substantial economic and business interests in Taiwan.
insights.locator: “Deeper commercial ties send a very clear message to China,”
